title: Hydrosphere Flashcards
description: Key facts from TNPSC Group II Geography Hydrosphere Chapter

cards.q: What percentage of the ocean area is occupied by the Continental Shelf?
What is the approximate depth limit of the Continental Shelf in fathoms and meters?
cards.a: 100 fathoms (180 meters).

cards.q: Why are the world's chief fishing grounds found in the Continental Shelf?
cards.a: Its shallowness allows sunlight to penetrate, fostering minute plants and microorganisms that provide food for marine life.

cards.q: Which is the deepest trench in the world and where is it located?
cards.a: Mariana Trench (Challenger Deep) in the West Pacific Ocean.

cards.q: What is the deepest trench in the Atlantic Ocean?
cards.a: Puerto Rico Trench (Milwaukee Deep).

cards.q: What is the Sargasso Sea known for?
cards.a: It is a calm sea in the North Atlantic full of Sargassum seaweeds, located within the circuit of North Atlantic currents.

cards.q: Which ridge divides the Mid-Atlantic Ridge into two parts near the equator?
cards.a: The Romanche Deep.

cards.q: What is the Ninety East Ridge?
cards.a: An important submarine ridge in the Indian Ocean running along the 90°E longitude.

cards.q: What are the major tidal energy potential sites in India and their capacities?
cards.a: Gulf of Khambhat (7000 MW), Gulf of Kutch (1000 MW), and Sunderbans (100 MW).

cards.q: Where is the wave energy harnessing plant located in India?
cards.a: Vizhinjam, near Thiruvananthapuram in Kerala.

cards.q: What is the minimum temperature difference required to produce Sea Thermal Power (OTEC)?
cards.a: 20°C between surface water and deep water (1000-3000m).

cards.q: Where are the two experimental geothermal energy projects located in India?
cards.a: Parvati Valley (Manikaran, HP) and Puga Valley (Ladakh, J&K).

cards.q: Where is the highest temperature of ocean water recorded?
cards.a: In tropical regions (23° to 27°C), not at the equator.

cards.q: What is the average salinity of the oceans?
cards.a: 35 parts per thousand (35‰).

cards.q: Which water body has the highest recorded salinity (330‰)?
cards.a: Lake Van in Turkey.

cards.q: Why does the Baltic Sea have very low salinity (11‰)?
cards.a: Due to a slow rate of evaporation and the influx of fresh water from many rivers and streams.

cards.q: What are Spring Tides?
cards.a: Tides that occur during New and Full Moons when the Sun, Moon, and Earth are in a straight line, causing the highest high tides and lowest low tides.

cards.q: What is a Tidal Bore?
cards.a: A steep-nosed tide crest that looks like a vertical wall of water rushing upstream in a narrow river estuary (e.g., Hooghly River).

cards.q: Which bay has the highest tidal range in the world (15-20 meters)?
cards.a: Bay of Fundy in Canada.

cards.q: What causes the thick fog near Newfoundland?
cards.a: The confluence of the warm Gulf Stream and the cold Labrador Current.

cards.q: What is the 'Monsoon Drift'?
cards.a: The ocean currents in the North Indian Ocean that change direction seasonally due to the monsoons.

cards.q: What are the three main types of coral reefs?
cards.a: Fringing Reef, Barrier Reef, and Atoll.

cards.q: Where is the largest Barrier Reef in the world located?
cards.a: Off the coast of Australia (Great Barrier Reef).

cards.q: What is Coral Bleaching?
cards.a: The loss of algae from corals resulting in a white color, indicating the death of corals (caused by global warming, El Niño, pollution).

cards.q: Which is the only cold desert in India?
cards.a: Ladakh.

cards.q: Where is the headquarters of the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA)?
cards.a: Chennai (established in 2003 under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002).
